pages.title: API reference
pages.summary: Every public class of WPToolkit, in the order to read them.

pages.title: Foundation
pages.summary: The kernel: one Application per plugin, its container and providers, the hooks it adds, and the prefixed names (Identity) everything else is built from.

pages.title: Application
pages.summary: One consuming plugin or theme. Owns its container, its hooks and its providers; nothing is static, so two plugins never share state (ADR-0007).

pages.title: ServiceProvider
pages.summary: Groups the wiring for one feature.

pages.title: Identity
pages.summary: Every name the library writes into WordPress's global namespace, derived from the consumer's slug, so two plugins — or two copies of WPToolkit — never collide (ADR-0005, ADR-0006).

pages.title: Config
pages.summary: Immutable configuration for one plugin or theme (replaces 0.x `Utils\Config`).

pages.title: HookRegistrar
pages.summary: Adds WordPress actions and filters for one plugin and remembers every one, so the plugin can list them (`hooks:list`) and remove all of them on deactivation. Replaces 0.x's `add_tracked_action()`.

pages.title: Container
pages.summary: The library's own container (ADR-0007): bindings, singletons, constructor autowiring, method injection, and an error that names the cycle when entries depend on each other.

pages.title: Coexistence
pages.summary: The coexistence ledger: every copy of WPToolkit loaded on the site records itself here, so a plugin can see which copies exist (`toolkit:info`, diagnostics) and explain a conflict.

pages.title: CopyOwner
pages.summary: Works out which plugin, must-use plugin or theme a WPToolkit copy was loaded from, so a conflict message can name it instead of leaving the administrator to decode a path.

pages.title: CoreServices
pages.summary: The services every application gets, as lazy singletons — nothing is built until something asks for it. Each can be rebound by a provider's register(), e.g. to swap the HttpClient.

pages.title: LibraryTranslations
pages.summary: Loads translations for the library's own strings (text domain `wptoolkit`) from the package's `languages/` directory — wherever the package lives, including a consumer's `vendor/` or a scoped copy (ADR-0006, ADR-0019).

pages.title: Psr11Bridge
pages.summary: Exposes the application container as PSR-11, for libraries that resolve services from one.

pages.title: ToolkitCompatibility
pages.summary: Checks the consumer's `requires_toolkit` constraint against the WPToolkit copy that is actually loaded, and explains a conflict in terms an administrator can act on (ADR-0005, ADR-0020).

pages.title: Http
pages.summary: One pipeline for REST, admin-ajax and public pages: the router and its fluent routes, requests and responses, and the dispatcher that enforces access, validation and rate limits.

pages.title: Router
pages.summary: Collects routes and registers them with WordPress — REST and/or admin-ajax — through the same Dispatcher (ADR-0008). Replaces 0.x `Ajax` and `RestRoute`.

pages.title: Route
pages.summary: One route, built fluently (Builder). Declares who may call it — there is no default (ADR-0008) — and how it's exposed.

pages.title: Request
pages.summary: An incoming request, the same shape whether it arrived over REST or admin-ajax (immutable).

pages.title: Response
pages.summary: An outgoing response, sent as JSON by either transport (immutable).

pages.title: HttpError
pages.summary: An error meant for the client: it carries the HTTP status, a stable machine-readable code and a message safe to show. Anything else thrown by a controller becomes a generic 500 (ADR-0008).

pages.title: Dispatcher
pages.summary: The one request pipeline both transports use (ADR-0008), so every security rule is written once:

pages.title: ApiClient
pages.summary: A client for one remote API (ports 0.x `APIHelper`): base URL, authentication, JSON, retries with backoff, cached GETs and logging — over any HttpClient (ADR-0004).

pages.title: Auth
pages.summary: How ApiClient authenticates each request (Strategy).

pages.title: AjaxTransport
pages.summary: Exposes routes through admin-ajax as `{slug}_{route}` actions. Logged-out access (`wp_ajax_nopriv_…`) is registered only for `->public()` routes; the Dispatcher still checks.

pages.title: RestTransport
pages.summary: Exposes routes on the WordPress REST API under the consumer's namespace (`my-plugin/v1`).
